title: Session transcript
description: One session: its identity, its turns, and the episode sets annotated over it. Written from docs/SPEC-gate0.md §5.1, §5.3 and §5.8. Turn-level field names match Sandpiper's (§10 item 3); everything above the turn is ours.

student_id.$comment: [SOURCE: docs/SPEC-gate0.md §5.8 — from the manifest supplied with the data, never inferred]

session_index.$comment: [SOURCE: docs/SPEC-gate0.md §5.8 — manifest-supplied order, never inferred from dates or file names]

session_date.$comment: [OURS: no format asserted. §5.8 leaves the manifest's date format open, and asserting date-time here would reject an intake file the spec permits.]

has_timestamps.$comment: [SOURCE: docs/SPEC-gate0.md §5.8 — true only when every turn has start_time and end_time. The validator checks the claim against the turns; the schema cannot.]

transcript_scope.$comment: Which value is required for reportability is config.session.requiredTranscriptScope, not this schema.

lead_role.$comment: [SOURCE: docs/SPEC-gate0.md §5.8 — supplied in the manifest, never inferred. Optional here: a demo set need not carry one.]

annotations.$comment: [SOURCE: docs/SPEC-gate0.md §5.3 — episodes are stored in the session-level annotations[] array, one tiling set per run. Absent on a raw intake transcript, which has no runs over it yet.]

problems.description: The problems worked on in this session, in turn order. An episode never straddles a boundary. Absent means the session was one problem.

start_time.$comment: [OURS: no format asserted; §5.8 does not fix one, and Sandpiper's transcripts carry offsets as well as clock times.]

annotations.$comment: Sandpiper's turn-level field, carried for compatibility at the turn level only (§10 item 3). Nothing in Gate 0 writes it; our episodes live on the session.

episode.description: A contiguous span of turns, spanning both speakers, during which the participants are doing one kind of problem-solving work. docs/SPEC-gate0.md §5.3.

episode_id.$comment: [SOURCE: docs/SPEC-gate0.md §5.3 — composed from the run id, the session and the ordinal within that session, so a later record can keep pointing at one episode.]

identifiedBy.$comment: Follows the run's kind, never set per episode (§5.3). The validator checks it against the run.

EPISODE.$comment: The code. Deliberately not an enum: the code list has exactly one home, codebook.v2.json, and the validator reads it from there for the run's codebook_version.

evidence.$comment: Exactly the turns of the span (§5.3, §9.1). The validator checks that; the schema cannot.

reviewer_id.$comment: Present and null in Gate 0 (§5.3). Neither presence nor nullness is required here: §9.1 gives each its own rejection, and a schema error would not name the offending episode.

tutor_prompting.$comment: Layer 2 (docs/SPEC-layer2.md). Nested because `codebook_version` above is the episode codebook's and this layer has its own.
